nodes.summary: `P(X ≥ k) = 0` for `k > n`.
nodes.title: Binomial upper tail vanishes beyond $n$

nodes.summary: The tail is nonincreasing in `k` for `p ∈ [0, 1]`.
nodes.title: The tail is nonincreasing in `k`

nodes.summary: `P(X ≥ 0) = 1`, for every real `p` (the binomial theorem).
nodes.title: Binomial upper tail at zero equals one

nodes.summary: The upper tail `P(X ≥ k) = ∑_{i = k}^{n} C(n, i) p^i (1 - p)^(n - i)` of the binomial law `Bin(n, p)`.
nodes.title: Upper tail of the binomial distribution

nodes.summary: The BLS of the empty set is `0`.
nodes.title: Branch length score of the empty set is zero

nodes.summary: The normalized BLS is at most `1` when the tree has positive total length.
nodes.title: Normalized branch length score is at most one for nonnegative lengths

nodes.summary: The normalized BLS is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Normalized branch length score is nonnegative for nonnegative lengths

nodes.summary: The normalized Branch Length Score, `bls S T w / totalLength T w`, as reported by Kheradpour et al. (a fraction of the total branch length).
nodes.title: Normalized branch length score

nodes.summary: The BLS is at most the total branch length.
nodes.title: Branch length score is at most the tree length for nonnegative lengths

nodes.summary: The BLS of the set of all leaves is the total branch length.
nodes.title: All species give the whole tree

nodes.summary: With nonnegative edge lengths, more conserving species never lower the BLS.
nodes.title: Monotonicity

nodes.summary: The BLS is nonnegative for nonnegative edge lengths.
nodes.title: Branch length score is nonnegative for nonnegative edge lengths

nodes.summary: A single species has BLS `0` (a motif present in one genome is not conserved).
nodes.title: A single species has BLS `0`

nodes.summary: For sets of species `S`, `S'` that share a species, the subtree connecting `S ∪ S'` is at most as long as the two subtrees together.
nodes.title: Subadditivity

nodes.summary: The Branch Length Score (unnormalized): the total branch length of the smallest subtree of `T` connecting the leaves `S`, as half the sum over the darts of the edge length times the indicator that `S` meets both sides (`edgeSide`) of the dart's edge.
nodes.title: The Branch Length Score

nodes.summary: A sum over darts of a function of the undirected edge is twice the sum over the edges: the two darts of each edge contribute equally.
nodes.title: Sum over darts is twice the sum over edges

nodes.summary: The taxa whose leaf is closer to the leaf vertex than to its neighbor are exactly that leaf's taxon.
nodes.title: The side of a pendant edge is the singleton of its leaf

nodes.summary: The `n log R` constant of Eq. 6.
nodes.title: Constant $n \log R$ term of the SiPhy objective

nodes.summary: For positive `c` and nonnegative `d` on a nonempty finite alphabet there is exactly one `γ` with `d b + γ > 0` for all `b` and `∑ b, c b / (d b + γ) = 1`.
nodes.title: The Lagrange multiplier of the `π` update exists and is unique

nodes.summary: The time-weighted exchange rate into `b`, `e b = ∑_{a ≠ b} τ a R a b`.
nodes.title: Time-weighted exchange rate into a state

nodes.summary: The rate update maximizes Eq. 6 over `ω > 0` for a fixed positive `π`, when the expected number of substitutions `N` and the time-weighted rate `∑ b, e b π b` are positive.
nodes.title: The rate update maximizes Eq. 6 over `ω > 0`

nodes.summary: Any other `ω > 0` gives a strictly smaller value of Eq. 6.
nodes.title: The rate update is the unique maximizer

nodes.summary: The constraint-vector update is the unique maximizer of Eq. 6 over the positive probability vectors `π` (the rate matrix `ω R π` and the root distribution both use `π`), for fixed `ω > 0`, positive off-diagonal `R` and positive weights `c`.
nodes.title: The constraint-vector update is the unique maximizer of Eq. 6

nodes.summary: For `ω > 0`, positive off-diagonal `R` and positive `π`, `expectedLogLik = N log ω + ∑_{a ≠ b} n a b log R a b + piObjective c (ω e) π`.
nodes.title: Eq. 6 for the SiPhy matrix

nodes.summary: The expected complete-data log-likelihood of a rate matrix `Q` and root distribution `π` (Garber et al. 2009, Eq. 6): `∑_{a ≠ b} n a b log Q a b + ∑ a, τ a Q a a + ∑ b, r b log π b`, for expected substitution counts `n`, expected state durations `τ` and the root posterior `r`.
nodes.title: The expected complete-data log-likelihood

nodes.summary: Derivative of the binomial upper tail in the success probability: for `1 ≤ k ≤ n`, `d/dp P(Bin(n, p) ≥ k) = n C(n - 1, k - 1) p^(k-1) (1-p)^(n-k)` at every real `p` (the sum telescopes).
nodes.title: Derivative of the binomial upper tail

nodes.summary: The weight `c b = ∑_{a ≠ b} n a b + r b` of state `b`: substitutions into `b` plus the root posterior of `b`.
nodes.title: Weight of a state: substitutions into it plus root posterior

nodes.summary: For symmetric `R` it is in detailed balance with `π`, for every `ω`.
nodes.title: `π` is the equilibrium of the SiPhy matrix

nodes.summary: With `ω ≥ 0`, nonnegative `R` and nonnegative `π`, the SiPhy matrix is a rate matrix.
nodes.title: SiPhy matrix is a rate matrix

nodes.summary: The MCS approximation is strictly increasing in the conserved count, for `N ≥ 1` and `p ∈ (0, 1)`.
nodes.title: Motif conservation score approximation is strictly increasing

nodes.summary: The MCS approximation of the number of conserved occurrences among the first `n` is the de Moivre–Laplace standardized sum.
nodes.title: Motif conservation score approximation as a de Moivre–Laplace sum

nodes.summary: The conserved count `k` of a motif with `N` occurrences, standardized under `Bin(N, p)`: `(k - N p) / √(N p (1 - p))`. This is an approximation to Xie et al.'s MCS, not their exact score.
nodes.title: Binomial z-score approximation to the motif conservation score

nodes.summary: The binomial upper tail is nondecreasing in `p` on `[0, 1]`, for every `n` and `k`.
nodes.title: The binomial upper tail is nondecreasing in `p` on `(0, 1)`

nodes.summary: Edge lengths are nonnegative: every dart's undirected edge has nonnegative length.
nodes.title: Nonnegative edge lengths of a tree

nodes.summary: The SiPhy rate update (Eq. 7, for fixed `π`): `ω = N / ∑ b, e b π b`.
nodes.title: The SiPhy rate update

nodes.summary: The `π` update is the unique maximizer of `piObjective c d` over the positive probability vectors: with `γ` as in `existsUnique_lagrange`, every other positive `π` summing to one has a strictly smaller objective than `b ↦ c b / (d b + γ)`.
nodes.title: The `π` update is the unique maximizer

nodes.summary: The part of Eq. 6 that depends on `π` (for fixed `ω`): `∑ b, (c b * log (π b) - d b * π b)`.
nodes.title: Part of the SiPhy objective depending on the constraint vector

nodes.summary: The SiPhy constraint-vector update (Eq. 8, for fixed `ω`): `π b = c b / (ω e b + γ)`, with `γ` the Lagrange multiplier of `existsUnique_lagrange`.
nodes.title: The SiPhy constraint-vector update

nodes.summary: Whether the leaf set `S` meets both sides of an edge with leaf set `B` below it, inside a tree with leaf set `U`: `S ∩ B` and `S ∩ (U \ B)` are nonempty.
nodes.title: Leaf set meeting both sides of a tree edge

nodes.summary: The SiPhy rate matrix `Q a b = ω R a b π b` for `a ≠ b` (Garber et al. 2009, Eq. 10), with rows summing to zero: `ω` times the GTR matrix with exchangeabilities `R` and base frequencies `π`.
nodes.title: The SiPhy rate matrix

nodes.summary: The binomial upper tail is strictly increasing in `p` on `[0, 1]` when `1 ≤ k ≤ n`.
nodes.title: The binomial upper tail is strictly increasing in `p` on `(0, 1)`

nodes.summary: If the conservation indicators of the occurrences are i.i.d. Bernoulli(`p`) with `0 < p < 1`, then for every `z`, `P(z ≤ MCS approximation of the first n occurrences)` tends to the standard normal mass of `[z, ∞)`.
nodes.title: De Moivre–Laplace for the MCS approximation

nodes.summary: The expected total number of substitutions `N = ∑_{a ≠ b} n a b`.
nodes.title: Expected total number of substitutions

nodes.summary: The total branch length: half the sum of the edge lengths over the darts, since each undirected edge is traversed once in each direction.
nodes.title: Total branch length of a tree

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
